submission.justification: Sensor-T2 has the best unirradiated resolution (~6.0 um at 150 um), but it is ruled out for the innermost layer. After 2e16 neq/cm^2 its hit efficiency is only 82.0%, against a requirement of at least 97%, because it can no longer be fully depleted. Of the two technologies that are radiation-qualified, Sensor-T1 (planar, 98.5% efficiency after irradiation) resolves much better than Sensor-T3 (3D, 99.2%): about 9.0 um versus 13.7 um at 150 um. T3 was worse at every thickness simulated (16.0 um at 50 um, 18.8 um at 300 um). For T1, I scanned thicknesses from 50 to 300 um. Resolution gets worse below about 115 um (9.9 um at 50 um) and above about 200 um (11.8 um at 300 um). Between about 125 and 200 um it is flat at roughly 8.7-9.1 um. Running the simulation twice at 125 um gave 8.69 and 9.02 um, so run-to-run noise is about 0.3 um and differences inside this range are not meaningful. I chose 150 um, the middle of the flat range, which agrees with the 2025 simulation summary (9.0 um). Caveats: the resolution simulation is for unirradiated sensors only. The efficiency figures come from a single fluence point (2e16 neq/cm^2), and the documents don't say whether that covers the full end-of-life fluence. The irradiation data also don't show whether efficiency depends on thickness.

requirements.requirement: Goal: best possible single-hit spatial resolution in the innermost layer
requirements.evidence: Best resolution among the radiation-qualified options: T1 at 150 um gives ~9.0 um (simulated, unirradiated), versus 13.7 um for T3. T1 is flat at ~8.7-9.1 um from 125 to 200 um, with ~0.3 um run-to-run noise. T2 (6.0 um) is better on paper but excluded by the radiation constraint.

requirements.requirement: Sensor must be one of the three technologies in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Sensor-T1, the planar standard-pitch sensor, is listed in candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: Sensor must be suitable for the innermost-layer radiation environment
requirements.evidence: T1 hit efficiency after 2e16 neq/cm^2 is 98.5% (requirement >= 97%; irradiation_testbeam_2026.md and query_irradiation). Caveat: this is the only fluence tested, the efficiency does not depend on thickness in the data, and the documents don't confirm that 2e16 is the end-of-life fluence.
150 um is within the allowed range.
